description: Shared benchmark corpus: 100 synthetic project memories for dualmem vs claude-mem comparison

memories.text: Chose PostgreSQL over MongoDB for the user service because we need ACID transactions for payment processing
The rate limiter in api/middleware.go intentionally skips nil checks on the hot path for performance. Do not add nil guards.
Rejected Redis for session storage, using encrypted JWT tokens instead to avoid single point of failure
In progress: migrating user service from REST to gRPC. Done: proto definitions, server scaffold. Remaining: client generation, integration tests
Do not upgrade to Go 1.23 yet - the new range-over-func feature breaks our custom iterator in collections/iter.go
Using OpenTelemetry for distributed tracing instead of Jaeger client library directly, for vendor neutrality
Auth refactor: completed JWT validation and middleware. Next up: refresh token rotation and logout endpoint
Adopted sqlc over raw SQL for type-safe database queries. Migration from hand-written queries started in services/user/
The WebSocket connection manager in ws/hub.go uses a global mutex. Under high load (>10k connections), switch to sharded locks
Frontend bundle size was 2.3MB. Switched from moment.js to dayjs, reducing to 1.1MB
Kubernetes migration: staging cluster deployed, Helm charts written. Production cutover scheduled for next sprint
Chose Viper for configuration management over envconfig due to hot-reload support and multi-source config merging
The batch processor in jobs/batch.go has an intentional 100ms sleep between batches to prevent database connection pool exhaustion
Using Protocol Buffers for inter-service communication. JSON only at the API gateway level for external clients
Search feature: Elasticsearch indexing complete, query API written. Remaining: autocomplete, fuzzy matching, pagination
Implemented circuit breaker pattern using sony/gobreaker for all external API calls to prevent cascade failures
tests/integration/ requires Docker to be running. CI uses testcontainers. Do not try to run integration tests without Docker.
Chose chi router over gorilla/mux because gorilla is archived and chi has better middleware composition
CI pipeline: GitHub Actions workflow written. Missing: security scanning (Snyk), artifact caching, deployment triggers
Using go-migrate for database migrations. Each migration is a pair of up/down SQL files in migrations/
The email service uses a connection pool with max 5 SMTP connections. Exceeding this causes silent message drops, not errors.
Adopted feature flags using LaunchDarkly for gradual rollout of the new checkout flow
API documentation: OpenAPI spec generated from code annotations. Remaining: examples, authentication section, webhook docs
Chose NATS over RabbitMQ for event bus because of simpler operational model and built-in clustering
services/user/cache.go uses a hand-rolled LRU cache. Do not replace with groupcache - we tested it and it doubled latency due to singleflight overhead on our workload
Using testify for test assertions instead of raw if-checks. All new tests should use require/assert from testify
Notification system: push notification service deployed. Remaining: email digests, in-app notifications, notification preferences UI
Implemented CQRS pattern for order processing: write model in PostgreSQL, read model in Elasticsearch for fast queries
The GraphQL resolver in api/graphql/resolver.go uses dataloader for N+1 prevention. Removing the dataloader causes exponential query growth.
Adopted Temporal for long-running workflows (order fulfillment, refunds) instead of custom state machines
Metrics dashboard: Grafana dashboards for API latency, error rates, DB connections. Missing: business metrics (revenue, conversion)
Using golangci-lint with custom config for linting. Disabled exhaustruct linter because it's too noisy with protobuf-generated code
The migration 20240315_add_indexes.sql takes 45 minutes on production data. Must run during maintenance window, not during deploy.
Chose zerolog over zap for structured logging because of zero-allocation design and simpler API
User analytics pipeline: Kafka events flowing, ClickHouse ingestion working. Remaining: retention queries, cohort analysis, dashboard
Implemented multi-tenant isolation using PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS) rather than separate databases per tenant
The file upload handler in api/upload.go streams directly to S3 without buffering to disk. Changing this to buffer first will OOM on large files.
Frontend state management: migrated from Redux to Zustand. Reduced boilerplate by 60% and simplified component testing
Payment integration: Stripe checkout working. Remaining: webhook handling, subscription management, invoice generation
Using ko for container image building instead of Dockerfile. Produces minimal images and integrates with go build
The cron scheduler in jobs/scheduler.go uses UTC internally. All cron expressions in config must be in UTC, not local time.
Implemented graceful shutdown with 30s timeout. All HTTP handlers check context cancellation. Background workers drain queues before exit.
API versioning: v2 endpoints created under /api/v2/. v1 deprecated but still serving. Full v1 sunset planned for Q3
Chose mTLS for service-to-service authentication. Certificates managed by cert-manager in Kubernetes.
The health check endpoint /healthz does a DB ping. If the DB is slow, the health check fails and K8s restarts the pod. Adjust probe timeout if DB is under load.
Using gomock for interface mocking in unit tests. Generated mocks live in mocks/ subdirectory of each package.
Localization: i18n framework integrated, English strings extracted. Remaining: Spanish, French, German translations, RTL support
Implemented API rate limiting per-tenant using sliding window algorithm stored in Redis
The CSV export in services/export/csv.go uses streaming writes. Do not load all rows into memory first - production exports can be 500MB+
Adopted semantic versioning for the API. Breaking changes increment major version. Internal services use date-based versions.
Using Wire for dependency injection instead of uber/fx because Wire generates code at compile time, no runtime reflection
The user search index rebuilds nightly at 3am UTC via cron. Manual reindex during peak hours will cause search latency spikes.
Chose Cloudflare R2 over AWS S3 for file storage due to zero egress fees and S3-compatible API
OAuth2 provider support: Google login working. Remaining: GitHub, Apple, SAML SSO for enterprise customers
Implemented database connection pooling with pgxpool. Max 25 connections per service instance, with health check pings every 30s.
The admin panel at /admin uses a separate auth flow with RBAC. Do not merge admin and user auth - they have different security requirements.
Frontend testing: Vitest for unit tests, Playwright for E2E. Dropped Cypress due to slower execution and higher resource usage.
Cache invalidation: Redis pub/sub for cache busting across instances. Remaining: cache warming on deploy, TTL tuning, cache metrics
Using GitHub Actions with self-hosted runners on ARM64 for faster CI. Build times reduced from 12 min to 4 min.
The PDF generation in services/report/pdf.go spawns a headless Chrome process. Max 3 concurrent renders or the server runs out of memory.
Implemented structured error handling with error codes. All API errors return {code, message, details} format.
Database sharding: shard key chosen (tenant_id), vitess cluster set up. Remaining: data migration, query routing, cross-shard queries
Chose Tailwind CSS over styled-components for the frontend. Better performance due to no runtime CSS-in-JS overhead.
The migration rollback in migrations/rollback.sh does NOT handle data loss gracefully. Always backup the database before running rollback.
Implemented request tracing with correlation IDs. Every HTTP request gets a unique trace ID in X-Request-ID header.
Audit logging: database triggers capture all writes. Remaining: audit log viewer UI, retention policy, compliance report generation
Using Buf instead of protoc for protobuf compilation. Better dependency management and breaking change detection.
The notification dispatcher uses a fan-out pattern with 10 worker goroutines. Increasing beyond 10 causes SMTP rate limiting from our email provider.
Frontend routing: React Router v6 with lazy loading for code splitting. Each route loads its own chunk.
Service mesh: Istio installed in staging. Remaining: production rollout, traffic policies, mTLS enforcement, Kiali dashboard
Chose Argo CD for GitOps deployment over Flux because of better UI and application-of-applications pattern
The S3 presigned URL generator in services/storage/presign.go caches URLs for 14 minutes (URLs expire in 15). Changing the cache TTL breaks the 1-minute safety margin.
Implemented blue-green deployment for zero-downtime releases. The deploy/blue-green.sh script handles traffic switching.
Performance testing: k6 scripts written for key endpoints. Remaining: load test in staging, establish baselines, set up continuous benchmarking
Using Docker Compose for local development. All services, databases, and message brokers defined in docker-compose.yaml
The GraphQL subscription handler in api/graphql/subscription.go leaks goroutines if clients disconnect without proper close frame. Added cleanup timer as workaround.
Implemented content-addressable storage for user uploads. Files are deduplicated by SHA-256 hash before storing to R2.
Error tracking: Sentry integrated for backend. Remaining: frontend Sentry, source maps upload, alert rules, PII scrubbing
Chose Renovate over Dependabot for automated dependency updates. Better monorepo support and grouping rules.
The test database in tests/fixtures/ is 200MB and tracked with Git LFS. Running git clone without LFS installed will break test fixtures.
Implemented event sourcing for the inventory service. All stock changes are events, current state rebuilt from event log.
Accessibility audit: screen reader testing complete. Remaining: keyboard navigation, ARIA labels, color contrast fixes, WCAG report
Using pgbouncer for connection pooling in production instead of application-level pooling for better connection reuse across pods
The webhook retry logic in services/webhook/retry.go uses exponential backoff with jitter. Max 5 retries over 24 hours. Changing retry count affects SLA guarantees.
Frontend form handling: React Hook Form with Zod validation. All form schemas defined in web/src/schemas/
Data pipeline: Airbyte connectors configured for CRM sync. Remaining: transformation layer (dbt), data warehouse setup (Snowflake), dashboards
Implemented soft deletes across all entities using deleted_at timestamp. Hard deletes only via admin API with audit trail.
The SSE (Server-Sent Events) endpoint in api/sse.go holds connections open indefinitely. Each connection consumes a goroutine. Monitor /debug/pprof/goroutine.
Chose Storybook for frontend component documentation and visual testing. All reusable components have stories.
Disaster recovery: RTO target 4 hours, RPO 1 hour. Cross-region DB replication configured. Remaining: automated failover, DR drills, runbook
Implemented request/response logging middleware that redacts sensitive fields (password, token, card_number) before logging
The DNS-based service discovery in pkg/discovery/dns.go caches results for 30s. Setting TTL lower than 30s has no effect due to Go's net.Resolver caching.
Using Terraform for infrastructure provisioning. State stored in Terraform Cloud. Modules in terraform/modules/.
Mobile app: React Native project initialized, auth flow working. Remaining: product listing, cart, checkout, push notifications
Adopted trunk-based development. All work goes to main via short-lived feature branches. Release branches cut weekly.
The image processing pipeline in services/media/resize.go uses cgo bindings to libvips. Building without libvips installed causes silent fallback to pure Go which is 10x slower.
Implemented canary deployments using Argo Rollouts. 5% traffic for 10 minutes, then 25%, then 100%.
Security hardening: OWASP top 10 mitigations applied. Remaining: penetration test, security headers audit, CSP policy, dependency scanning
Using GitHub Packages for private Go modules instead of a self-hosted proxy. GOPRIVATE configured for github.com/acme/*
The background job queue in jobs/queue.go uses SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. This only works on PostgreSQL 9.5+. Do not try to use it with SQLite or MySQL.
